beats.caption: HBM stacks beside the GPU hold its working data
beats.text: An AI accelerator keeps weights and activations in HBM, stacks of DRAM dies next to the GPU. Each die has many banks, and each bank can have only one row open at a time.

beats.caption: A bank with row 2 open: the row buffer holds its data
beats.text: An earlier ACTIVATE raised row 2's wordline. The sense amps drove every bitline to a full 0 or 1 and the row buffer now holds the whole row. Reads of that row are fast, but no other row in this bank can be reached.

beats.caption: PRECHARGE first restores the row into its cells
beats.text: Reading a DRAM cell drains its charge, so the data lives only in the sense amps after ACTIVATE. Before the row closes, the sense amps drive full-strength charge back into every cell of the row. That write-back is what keeps the bits from being lost.

beats.caption: Then the wordline drops and bitlines settle to half voltage
beats.text: The wordline falls, sealing each capacitor, and every bitline pair is shorted to half the supply voltage. A bitline sitting at the midpoint is what lets the next row's tiny charge tip it up or down. The time this takes is tRP, about 14 ns in modern DRAM.

beats.caption: Only now can the bank open another row
beats.text: A new ACTIVATE (row 6 here) can start once tRP has passed. Random access that keeps jumping rows pays PRECHARGE plus ACTIVATE every time, so controllers reorder requests to hit already-open rows. Related: Micron (MU), SK hynix (000660.KS), Rambus (RMBS).
